title: Looping and bounded retries
summary: A loop re-invokes an agent until a completion condition holds (marker, todos done, background tasks done, AI judge or your own callback), always with a maximum. It is experimental.
useIf: One run often stops early and you want the agent to keep working until a checkable condition is met, within a hard cap.
avoidIf: The condition cannot be checked cheaply and reliably, or one run is normally enough. Never loop without a cap.

explain.md: `LoopAgent` (.NET) wraps any `AIAgent`; `AgentLoopMiddleware` (Python) plugs into a regular `Agent`. After each invocation an **evaluator** decides whether to continue. The default maximum is **10 invocations**; Python judge loops default to **5**. The loop stops and returns when a tool approval is pending. The docs warn: always bound autonomous loops, because a completion condition can fail, a model can stall and an evaluator can be probabilistic [[tr9]].

explain.caption: Completion conditions (.NET evaluator names, Python equivalent in brackets)
head: Evaluator
Continues while
Cost profile
rows: The reply lacks a marker such as DONE
Free, brittle if the model forgets the marker
Todos remain, optionally only in selected modes
A separate judge says the request is not fully answered
One extra model call per iteration, judge sees your data
Your callback returns continue, optionally with feedback

explain.md: **Context control.** By default one session is reused and the winning evaluator's feedback becomes the next input. `FreshContextPerIteration` (.NET) or `fresh_context=True` (Python) restarts each pass from the original request plus a progress log and restores the session snapshot. Non-streaming runs return an aggregated transcript unless `NonStreamingReturnsLastResponseOnly` / `return_final_only=True`. Pass `max_iterations=None` only when the predicate is guaranteed to terminate [[tr9]].

blocks.code:
from agent_framework import Agent, AgentLoopMiddleware

def needs_more_work(*, last_result, iteration, **kwargs):
    if iteration >= 5:               # belt and braces on top of max_iterations
        return False
    return 'DONE' not in last_result.text   # or (True, 'feedback text')

agent = Agent(client=client,
              middleware=[AgentLoopMiddleware(needs_more_work, max_iterations=5)])

# judge-driven variant (default 5 iterations):
loop = AgentLoopMiddleware.with_judge(judge_client,
    criteria=['Answer every part of the request.'], max_iterations=4)

explain.title: Experimental (checked 2026-10-13)
explain.md: Agent looping is marked experimental. Only use a judge endpoint you trust with the original request and the generated response [[tr9]].

whereToUse: Execute-mode Harness runs that must finish every todo
Drafts that need a quality bar: loop with a judge until the criteria pass or the cap hits
Agents that delegate to background child tasks and must wait for all of them
Retry-with-feedback for outputs that must contain a required structure

use: The stop condition is cheap and checkable: todos, marker, test result
A cap and a cost ceiling per run are acceptable
A second pass really improves the result more than it costs
avoid: The only evaluator is another model with the same blind spots
No cap: a stuck condition means unbounded cost
The task is deterministic: use a workflow loop edge with an explicit exit test
flips: Judge rarely says done: reduce criteria, lower the cap or replace the judge with a code check
Iterations grow context: switch to fresh context per iteration with a progress log

pitfalls.symptom: Cost per request is 10 times the single-run cost
pitfalls.cause: The condition never becomes true and the loop runs to the default cap of 10
pitfalls.fix: Lower `max_iterations`, fix the condition, monitor iterations per request

pitfalls.symptom: A loop ends silently while an approval is pending
pitfalls.cause: The loop stops and returns when a tool approval is pending
pitfalls.fix: Handle `user_input_requests` or approval content after the loop returns and resume with the same session

pitfalls.cause: The judge client receives the original request and the generated response
pitfalls.fix: Use a judge endpoint in the same trust and data boundary

scenarios.title: Finish all todos, bounded
scenarios.situation: A Harness agent works through 15 todos in execute mode but returns after 4 to 6 of them. Users want completion without babysitting. A run costs about 0.40 in tokens.
constraints: Cost cap of about 3 per request
unknowns: Is the early stop a model habit or a context problem?
Can the cap be 6 or 7 iterations?
scenarios.question: How do you get completion?

options.name: Todo-completion loop limited to execute mode, cap of 7 iterations
options.why: A free, exact condition. 7 iterations x 0.40 is about 2.80, under the 3.00 cap.
options.tradeoff: Experimental API, and incomplete work is returned if the cap hits.

options.name: AI judge loop
options.why: Adds a model call per iteration for a condition the todo list answers exactly.
options.tradeoff: Right for fuzzy quality criteria with no checkable state.

options.name: Remove the cap
options.why: A stuck condition becomes unbounded cost.
options.tradeoff: Acceptable only when the predicate is guaranteed to terminate.

flips.then: Add a short judge for the final answer on top of the todo condition.
Enable fresh context per iteration with a progress log.

scenarios.takeaway: Prefer exact conditions over judges, and compute the worst-case bill from the cap.

scenarios.title: Quality bar for a customer letter
scenarios.situation: Letters must cover five required points. A quality reviewer rejects 30 percent of first drafts. Letters are not time critical.
unknowns: Can the points be checked in code?
Is a judge allowed to see the letter?
scenarios.question: What loop do you build?

options.name: A delegate evaluator that checks the five points in code and returns feedback, cap of 3
options.why: Exact, free and gives targeted feedback; confidential text stays in your process.
options.tradeoff: You write and maintain the checks.

options.name: A judge model in the same data boundary with criteria
options.why: Flexible for softer criteria such as tone.
options.tradeoff: Extra cost per iteration and probabilistic verdicts.

options.name: A judge on a public endpoint
options.why: The judge receives the request and response, which are confidential.

flips.if: Tone matters as much as coverage
flips.then: Use code checks first, then a judge for tone with a lower cap.

flips.if: Letters are generated in bulk overnight
flips.then: A higher cap is affordable, still bound it.

scenarios.takeaway: Check what you can in code, judge only what you must, and keep the judge inside your data boundary.

quiz.q: A looped agent run costs 0.50 per iteration and the judge adds 0.10 per iteration. With the Python judge-loop default of 5 iterations, what is the worst-case cost per request?
quiz.explain: 5 iterations x (0.50 + 0.10) = 3.00. A cap turns an open-ended loop into a known worst case.

quiz.q: Which statements about looping are true? Select all.
options: The default maximum is 10 agent invocations
The loop stops and returns when a tool approval is pending
Looping is a stable, GA feature in every SDK
`max_iterations=None` is safe whenever you trust the model
quiz.explain: Looping is experimental and absent in Go, and `None` is only for predicates guaranteed to terminate.

flashcards.front: What is the default loop cap?
flashcards.back: 10 agent invocations (`LoopAgent`, `AgentLoopMiddleware`). Python judge loops default to 5.

flashcards.front: Name three loop evaluators besides a judge.
flashcards.back: Completion marker, todo completion, background-task completion, or a delegate callback.

flashcards.front: What does fresh context per iteration do?
flashcards.back: Rebuilds each pass from the original request plus a progress log and restores the session snapshot, so context does not grow.
